name: Numenor
note: Fan work from Tolkien, whose world belongs to the Tolkien Estate; nothing from any book, film or game is used. The whole island at true proportion, generated by tools/make-numenor.py from the published geography: about seven hundred kilometres from the tip of one promontory to the tip of the next but one. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin at the Meneltarma, so one degree of latitude is 111,132 m and one of longitude 111,320 m.
attribution: Numenor is fan work: land generated by tools/make-numenor.py. Tolkien's world belongs to the Tolkien Estate. No assets used.

numenor._: src/numenor/: the land cover, the forests, the rivers, the surf, the ships and the eagles

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: The Meneltarma
landmarks.info: The Pillar of Heaven, in the midst of the island: grass on its long lower slopes, steeper as it climbs, and a flat summit with nothing built on it. The Hallow of Eru, open to the sky, where the King spoke for the people three times a year and no one else spoke at all. A road goes up it in a spiral from the north-east. Its height is ours: no figure is given.

landmarks.name: Armenelos
landmarks.info: The City of Kings, on its hill east of the mountain. The King's House stands in its court with a tall tower, and before it the White Tree, Nimloth, the gift of the Eldar, which flowers white and is fragrant at dusk. Every building here is our own; the texts give the city a court, a tower and a tree, not a plan.

landmarks.name: The Temple
landmarks.info: The temple Sauron had raised in Armenelos when the Faithful were persecuted: a drum of dark stone with a silver dome gone black with smoke, and the louver at its top always smoking. The White Tree had been cut down to feed its first fire. Its shape is ours, from the description of its size only.

landmarks.name: Romenna
landmarks.info: The great haven of the east, at the head of its firth: the port of the King's Road and of the ships that sailed for Middle-earth. It faces east, toward the lands Numenor went back to.

landmarks.name: Tol Uinen
landmarks.info: An island in the Firth of Romenna, and the tower of Calmindon on it, built to watch the ships come and go.

landmarks.name: Andunie
landmarks.info: The haven of the west, facing the sunset and the land that cannot be seen from it. Its lords were the Elf-friends; the Elvish ships put in here.

landmarks.name: Eldalonde
landmarks.info: The Green Haven, at the head of the Bay of Eldanna, among the Nisimaldar: evergreen woods of fragrant trees, brought over the sea by the Eldar, that never lose their leaves.

landmarks.name: Nindamos
landmarks.info: The fishing town at the mouth of the Siril, among the marshes and the lagoons of its delta.

landmarks.name: The Noirinan
landmarks.info: The Valley of Tombs, at the south-west foot of the Meneltarma, where the Kings and Queens lie in tombs cut into the rock.

landmarks.name: Sorontil
landmarks.info: The great cliff on the north coast of Forostar, where the eagles nest.

landmarks.name: Ondosto
landmarks.info: The town of Forostar, near its border with Orrostar: the stone-workers', in the stony north.

landmarks.name: Hyarastorni
landmarks.info: The shipwrights' town on the coast of Hyarrostar, where the great forests come down to the sea. (The name is ours for this place.)

landmarks.name: Moriondë
landmarks.info: The harbour of Orrostar's north coast. (A name we have given it.)

landmarks.name: Nisinen
landmarks.info: The lake on the course of the Nunduine, west of the mountain, in its reeds and its marshes.

landmarks.name: Emerie
landmarks.info: The sheep-country of Mittalmar: rolling downs, the grass close-cropped, a long way from the sea.

landmarks.name: The Siril
landmarks.info: The chief river of the island, south from the mountain to the sea at Nindamos.
